issues.detail: The Guidelines mix unrelated one-off notes (Groq Whisper transcription, RAM figures, env var patterns, migration tips) into a long list, and the Instructions pack in many peripheral details.

scenarios.name: telegram-bot-on-pi-with-secrets-split
scenarios.rationale: Response A matches nearly every rubric item: checksum-verified arm64 archive, onboard, model_list with model_name, channel_list.telegram with allow_from, secrets in .security.yml with chmod 600, and gateway/status. Response B guesses at an outdated config format, puts secrets in config.json, skips checksum verification, and uses a bare binary download.

scenarios.name: docker-discord-nightly-summary
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric closely: launcher profile to generate config, then gateway with up -d, discord allow_from, .security.yml, a Discord DM request for the schedule, cron/ storage and picoclaw cron list; A declines to give any PicoClaw-specific setup and offers only generic Compose and host-cron placeholders.

scenarios.name: safe-heartbeat-and-cron-hardening
scenarios.rationale: Response B covers nearly every rubric item (heartbeat interval 60 with HEARTBEAT.md and the 5-minute minimum, allow_from with specific IDs, restrict_to_workspace true, empty command_allowed_remotes never "*", and enable_deny_patterns), while Response A refuses to use PicoClaw's config keys and gives only generic advice with a separate cron script.
